issues.problem: The default Codex transcript directory is the predictable ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sb-codex-transcripts.<uid>.<pid>. It is created with `mkdir -p` (an existing directory is accepted, whoever owns it), a failing `chmod 700` is ignored (the call runs inside `$(... 2>/dev/null || true)`), and the files are then written with `open('w')` / `cp -f` / `>`, which follow symlinks. With TMPDIR unset (the Linux default) /tmp is shared: another local user can pre-create the directory and plant latest.jsonl as a symlink, which makes the victim overwrite any file they own with the raw prompt and transcript. Planting a world-writable regular file instead lets the attacker read the raw transcript. fs.protected_symlinks does not help, because the planted directory is not sticky. Redaction refuses the symlink, so the clobbered content stays unredacted. The directory is never removed after the run either, so each delegation leaves a new transcript directory in /tmp (undocumented).
issues.evidence: Probe REVF-G6b-r2-probe/victim.sh: victim uid 65534 (setpriv), TMPDIR=<shared 1777 dir>. The attacker (root standing in for another user) pre-creates sb-codex-transcripts.65534.<victim pid> 0777 with latest.jsonl -> victim's ~/.bashrc and a 0666 latest.meta.json, then the victim runs codex_capture_transcript. Output: 'chmod: changing permissions of .../sb-codex-transcripts.65534.26017: Operation not permitted', 'ERROR: refusing to redact through a symlink', and the victim's .bashrc now holds '{"type": "prompt.submitted", "prompt": "my private prompt\n"}' plus the transcript line. The attacker-owned meta file (still 0666) holds work_dir and source paths. fs.protected_symlinks=0 here, but the attack does not depend on it.
issues.suggested_fix: Create the per-run directory with `mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sb-codex-transcripts.XXXXXX"` (0700, unpredictable). If CODEX_TRANSCRIPT_DIR is given, refuse a directory that is a symlink, is not owned by the user or is group/world-writable. Write files with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW (or to a temp file plus rename) and fail closed, writing no transcript, if any of this fails. Document that the directory persists (or remove it at the end and drop the archived-path line). Add a test that a pre-existing foreign or symlinked directory is refused.

issues.problem: The new 'not a code reference' exemptions classify any [A-Za-z0-9_] value that contains an underscore as an identifier, whatever its digits or entropy. Dotted runs of random segments count as attribute chains, and letters-only values need 24+ characters and entropy ≥ 4.3. As a result the brief scanner (the gate before a brief reaches a third-party CLI) no longer catches literal secrets it caught at the r1 head. The r1 suggested fix limited this to identifiers WITHOUT digits.
issues.evidence: python3 -I REVF-G6b-r2-probe/scan_battery.py (68322a5 vs fbf2842 agent_redact.py). Now missed (each caught at r1): 'stripe_api_key: sk_test_<REDACTED-example-key>', 'API_KEY=Xk9_aP2mQ7vR4tL8nB3cW5', 'Authorization: Bearer abc_def_ghi_jkl_mno_pqr', 'API_KEY=Ab3.Xy9.Qw7.Er5.Ty1.Ui3', 'client_secret=hJkLqWeRtYuIoPaSdFgZ'. Also missed before and now: 'STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_51H8…', 'rk_live_…' (the name ends in secret_key, which _NAME does not list; there is no sk_live_/rk_ prefix rule) and Slack webhook URLs. Still caught: AWS AKID and secret, ghp_/gho_/github_pat_, PEM (RSA/EC/OPENSSH), JWT, xoxb-, Google, sk-/sk-proj-/sk-ant-, npm_, hf_, SendGrid, Twilio hex, URL userinfo, JSON-quoted password.
issues.suggested_fix: Exempt underscore identifiers only when they contain no digits (or when every underscore-separated segment reads as a word: letters only, low entropy). Treat dotted chains as references only when each segment is a word-like identifier. Add prefix rules for Stripe (sk_live_/sk_test_/rk_live_/rk_test_), Slack webhooks (hooks.slack.com/services/) and names ending in secret_key/secretkey. Pin each regressed sample in tests/python/test_agent_redact.py.

issues.location: scripts/lib/agent-delegate-common.sh:117-121 (agent_delegate_workdir_fingerprint), called before every attempt (agent-*-delegate.sh, e.g. codex:208)
issues.problem: `git hash-object -- "$f"` runs on every untracked path and follows symlinks. An untracked symlink to /dev/zero, a FIFO or /dev/stdin hangs the delegation before launch with no bound. A large non-ignored untracked file is hashed on every delegation, even though the fingerprint matters only for a quota retry. It also hashes files outside the work dir through symlinks.
issues.evidence: Probe: git repo with `ln -s /dev/zero zero-link`; `timeout 10 bash fp.sh` (source agent-delegate-common.sh; agent_delegate_workdir_fingerprint) -> rc=124 after 10.0 s; without the link, 0.1 s.
issues.suggested_fix: Hash only regular, non-symlink files (`[[ -f $f && ! -L $f ]]`); for symlinks, hash the readlink target string. Skip or size-cap huge files, or put a timeout on the whole fingerprint.

issues.problem: The scanner still rejects ordinary briefs: URL userinfo is flagged even when the password is an env reference or a local default credential, a prose mention of a PEM header is flagged, and a csrf_token set to a UUID is flagged. The refusal text tells the agent how to set SB_AGENT_ALLOW_SECRET_LIKE_BRIEF=1, so these false positives train routine use of the override, which nothing records except stderr.
issues.evidence: scan_battery.py false positives: 'DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/test' -> url-userinfo; 'git clone https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}@github.com/org/repo' -> url-userinfo; 'Never commit files that start with <PEM-header-redacted> markers.' -> pem; 'csrf_token = 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000' -> assignment.
issues.suggested_fix: Apply the reference checks (_ENV_REF, placeholders) to the userinfo password. Require a PEM body line after the header. Exempt UUID-shaped values. Record override use in the delegation log or state, so it leaves an audited trace.

issues.problem: The known-limit holds (the scoped run exits 0 and the effect is asserted), but its reason is not substantiated. 'drops the record for the first command of this particular substitution' does not say why, and the r1 code used the same `cd "$SB_ROOT" && \` form as opencode.sh, which the entry itself says is attributed. The line can be made measurable instead of excluded, for example by moving the launcher into a function (`codex_run_tui_launcher() { cd "$SB_ROOT" || return 1; ...; }`, output="$(codex_run_tui_launcher)") or by giving python a cwd. As written, the `cd` also has no failure handling (the launcher would run from the caller's directory).
issues.evidence: Scoped coverage report: 'Known limits (1 audited statements excluded…) scripts/lib/agent-adapters/codex.sh:380 (cd) [unmeasurable]'; git diff fbf2842..27518a6 shows the `cd … && \` form was replaced to produce this line.
issues.suggested_fix: Restructure into a function with `cd … || return 1`, cover it, and drop the known-limits entry; or explain the tracer mechanism precisely in the entry.

issues.problem: The reader fix leaves a small window: if select() times out, the CLI writes its last chunk and exits, and then `elif proc.poll() is not None: break` runs, the loop ends without draining, and that chunk is lost. The window is much smaller than the original bug, but it is the same class.
issues.evidence: Static (lines 211-222). The old reader lost output 6/30 times; this window was not hit in 30 runs.
issues.suggested_fix: When poll() reports an exit, drain the pipe non-blocking until EOF (or EAGAIN) before breaking.
